observations: A blocky rectangular head fills most of the frame, outlined in thick black lines against a near-black background, with the top edge cropped so the crown is cut off.
Two concentric-circle eyes sit asymmetrically: the left eye is larger and more fully rendered with a white highlight dot at center; the right eye is smaller and pushed toward the upper-right corner.
The lower half is dominated by a wide rectangular mouth zone built from stacked horizontal bands; white triangular tooth shapes alternate with black zigzag lines across two rows.
reading: The face pushes forward, its cropped crown and off-center eyes giving the whole structure a lopsided weight. Dense crosshatched strokes in lime, teal, red, and yellow pack every surface, yet the thick black outlines hold the geometry firm. The stacked tooth bands read as both grin and grid. What could feel threatening softens into something closer to bewildered.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between 'nnxyz nifty faces #26' and 'nnxyz nifty faces #28' in both title order and recorded creation order. All three share the rectangular face schema, but this is the only one in the owned subset cropped at the crown and set against a near-black ground.

connections.reason: Both use a blocky rectangular head with concentric-circle eyes and a toothed mouth band, but #26 fills the full frame on a light ground and adds ear-like side panels absent in #27.
nnxyz #31 shares paired spiral eyes and a horizontal zigzag tooth row in white against a dark band, making it a cross-collection echo of the same recurring face structure.

lookingQuestion: The two eyes are drawn at noticeably different sizes and heights — what does that asymmetry do to the stability of the face as a whole?
ambiguities: The crown of the head is cropped; it is unclear whether this reflects a canvas boundary or a choice to enlarge the face within the frame.
